conference.name: International Conference on Autonomous Systems
conference.tagline: From theory to practice: researchers present new ideas, and practitioners teach the tools that make autonomous systems work.

news.text: The Call for Papers is out: 5 speaking slots for papers with workshop and 8 for papers without workshop.

calls.title: Papers with Workshop

calls.title: Papers without Workshop

submissionRequirements.title: Title & Abstract
submissionRequirements.text: A concise title and an abstract (max 300 words).

submissionRequirements.title: Session Track
submissionRequirements.text: Clear indication of Paper with Workshop or Paper without Workshop.

submissionRequirements.title: Outline & Schedule
submissionRequirements.text: A breakdown of how the allotted time will be used.
items: Papers with workshop: detailed breakdown of the 25-minute morning session and milestone-based progression for the 90-minute workshop.
Papers without workshop: clear breakdown of the 15-minute presentation structure.

submissionRequirements.title: Prerequisites & Toolchain (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: List of required software, target OS compatibility, hardware dependencies, and recommended skill level.

submissionRequirements.title: Workshop Size (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: Choose a workshop for 25 or 50 participants. If the workshop needs equipment, prepare 10 sets for 25 participants or 20 sets for 50 participants.

submissionRequirements.title: Participant Hardware Requirements (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: The minimum hardware participants' laptops must meet, such as CPU, memory (RAM), GPU, free disk space and operating system. These requirements are published to attendees.

submissionRequirements.title: Teaching Assistant (Papers with Workshop)
submissionRequirements.text: At least one teaching assistant (TA) to help participants during the practical part of the workshop.

submissionRequirements.title: Interactive Demo Video (Papers with Workshop only)
submissionRequirements.text: A short demonstration video (2–5 minutes) showcasing the functioning prototype, project workflow, or target outcomes participants will build during the workshop.
items: Please provide a publicly viewable or unlisted link (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, or Google Drive).
This video is crucial for the program committee to evaluate technical feasibility and participant engagement.

submissionRequirements.title: Speaker Bio
submissionRequirements.text: Professional background (max 150 words), previous speaking experience, and relevant project links (e.g., GitHub, Google Scholar, LinkedIn).

reviewCriteria.title: Technical Depth & Originality
reviewCriteria.text: Novelty of the research or practical value of the tooling.

reviewCriteria.title: Clarity & Feasibility
reviewCriteria.text: Feasibility of completing the agenda within the allotted time frame (particularly for 90-minute workshops).

reviewCriteria.title: Engagement Plan
reviewCriteria.text: Degree of meaningful interactivity planned for workshop participants.

reviewCriteria.title: Theme Alignment
reviewCriteria.text: Relevance to current industry and academic trends.

items.q: What can I submit to ICAS?
items.a: Two kinds of proposals: Papers with Workshop (5 speaking slots), which engage the audience interactively through a presentation and a workshop, and Papers without Workshop (8 speaking slots), which present academic work relevant to the conference theme.

items.q: What is the difference between the two tracks?
items.a: Speakers of papers with workshop give a 25-minute presentation in the morning and run a 90-minute workshop in the afternoon. Speakers of papers without workshop give a talk of about 15 minutes in sessions that run concurrently with the afternoon workshops.

The paper as one PDF file (max 10 MB), a title and an abstract of at most 300 words, the session track, an outline and schedule, and a speaker bio of at most 150 words with previous speaking experience and relevant project links. Papers with workshop also need the prerequisites and toolchain, the workshop size, the laptop hardware requirements for participants, the teaching assistant(s) and a 2–5 minute demo video.

Yes. Proposals undergo double-blind peer review on technical depth and originality, clarity and feasibility, the engagement plan, and alignment with current industry and academic trends. Keep names and affiliations out of the paper, title, abstract and outline.

items.q: Do I have to use the ICAS slide template?
items.a: Yes. All speakers of accepted papers, with or without workshop, must prepare their slides with the official ICAS slide template, available on the Downloads page.

items.q: How does the 40% speaker feedback work?
items.a: Speakers of papers with workshop receive feedback based on attendance: 40% of the registration fees of their workshop. An engaging topic that draws more participants results in more feedback.

items.q: How large is a workshop, and who provides the equipment?
items.a: Speakers choose a workshop for 25 or 50 participants and prepare all equipment and environment set-ups: 10 equipment sets for 25 participants or 20 sets for 50 participants, if the workshop needs equipment. Attendees bring their own laptops.

Speakers provide the laptop hardware requirements of their workshop (for example CPU, memory, GPU, disk space and operating system), and they are published on the workshop pages. Please check them before registering for a workshop.

items.q: Do I need a teaching assistant?
items.a: Yes. Each workshop should have at least one teaching assistant (TA) to help participants during the practical part.
Registration opens after the notification of acceptance. Dates are listed on the Important Dates page; subscribe to updates to be notified.

items.q: Do participants register separately for workshops?
items.a: Yes. Workshop seats are registered separately from the conference registration and are limited to the workshop size chosen by the speakers.

items.q: Where and when will the conference take place?
items.a: The venue and dates will be announced on this website and in the site header.
